kata.name: Factory-method dispatch near-floor control - a two-kind creator where the sampled scripted dispatch test catches both the unrouted kind and the fall-through to the default
kata.series_report: docs/ref/pattern-kata-dispositions.md Factory Method row (disposed; construction dispatch); fixtures/katas/factory-method/README.md (pre-registered); beads catherine-r5k.2
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered: at the two-kind floor the sampled scripted test catches both injected faults, so the dispatch-agreement law buys zero unique detections (killed)

expected.detail: route(text) is null: the switch has no arm for the sampled kind. The conventional test observes an unrouted kind and the kernel emits an executed dangling route cell for the same kind - parity, not a lens win

handler(r_text) resolves to create_default while creator(text) is create_text: the conventional test observes the wrong concrete class and the kernel emits an executed equation violation on the same kind - parity

commands: python3 prototype/factory_method_baseline.py --assert  # exit 0: baseline arm frozen; both floor faults caught
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/factory-method/floor/dispatch.ct.json --json  # exit 0, findings []
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/factory-method/floor/fault-missing-route.ct.json --json  # exit 4, 1 dangling
cargo run -q -p catherine-cli -- check fixtures/katas/factory-method/floor/fault-silent-default.ct.json --json  # exit 3, 1 violation

comparison.conventional_baseline: the scripted factory test over both floor kinds: call the creator's dispatch and assert the returned concrete creator/class against the frozen expectation. Both floor faults change a sampled kind's observable class, so the baseline catches them.

baseline.artifact: prototype/factory_method_baseline.py sha256:62553030b06c98d87d43bed081b1d857b2d41fb9d243d63bf17ee93e0cbf3848 (scripted sampled factory dispatch test; always executed before the probe arm)

expressibility_gap.invariant: a live default arm is distinguishable from an intentional default
expressibility_gap.why: the control's two fault classes are behavior-changing and share the same shape as an intentional fallback; separating them needs a declared creator role (the separately pre-registered H2 entry), not the dispatch tables alone

procedure: 1. The fault set and its expectations were committed in fixtures/katas/factory-method/ (README.md, faults.json) before any recorded run; nothing here is edited after the run.

2. The baseline arm (prototype/factory_method_baseline.py, sha256 above) was executed first: a scripted dispatch test over the pre-registered sampled kinds, asserting the resolved concrete creator against the frozen expectation; kinds outside the sample are never inspected.
3. The probe arm ran the committed fixtures through the real CLI: `catherine check --json` over the clean floor and both fault variants.
4. Witnesses were mapped to presentation elements kind:<k> by the witness row over the declared alphabetical ProductKind rows; the two floor faults resolve to the sampled kind text.
5. Zero unique detections -> the control self-negates: verdict killed, no advantage at the two-kind floor.
